free_simple_company_search.description:
Searching the shared free company corpus with a constrained where_sql expression over the companies schema. | Run a single read-only SQL statement against the shared Snowflake-backed free company corpus (~35M companies).
Schema (table: companies):
normalized_domain text — lowercase root domain (e.g. 'openai.com')
domain text — original domain as-is
company_name text — company name (NOT NULL)
industry text — e.g. 'computer software', 'financial services', 'hospital & health care'
location text — comma-separated: locality, region, country (e.g. 'san francisco, california, united states')
linkedin_url text — LinkedIn company URL slug
employee_count integer — upper bound of size bucket (10, 50, 200, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000+)
year_founded integer — e.g. 2015
updated_at timestamp
Guidance:
Prefer exact company resolution with normalized_domain when you have a website/domain.
Exact normalized_domain equality/IN lookups are the fastest path for known domains.
Use linkedin_url and company_name equality/IN for small lookup batches; very large batches may still hit the query timeout.
If an exact lookup misses, use anchored prefix searches such as company_name ILIKE 'acme%' to generate fallback candidates.
Plain ILIKE '%keyword%' over broad fields is legal SQL on the Snowflake-backed corpus, but it can still scan the 35M-row table.
Use dedicated company search providers when you need provider-native facets, live web coverage, or strict market sizing totals.
Verify the returned company before assuming it is the same entity.
Example queries:
SELECT * FROM companies WHERE normalized_domain = 'openai.com' LIMIT 5
SELECT * FROM companies WHERE normalized_domain IN ('openai.com','anthropic.com') LIMIT 10
SELECT * FROM companies WHERE linkedin_url IN ('linkedin.com/company/openai') LIMIT 5
SELECT * FROM companies WHERE company_name ILIKE 'nestle%' LIMIT 10
SELECT * FROM companies WHERE industry = 'computer software' AND employee_count > 50 LIMIT 100
SELECT industry, count(*) as cnt FROM companies GROUP BY industry ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 25
SELECT * FROM companies WHERE location ILIKE 'san francisco%' AND year_founded >= 2020 LIMIT 100
Supports SELECT, aggregates, GROUP BY, WITH CTEs, and EXPLAIN. SQL must include LIMIT <= 100000.
Best for company retrieval, shortlist building, exact segment counts, and domain-to-company recovery when exact lookups miss.

bounceban_verify_single.description: Verify one email address before sending. Read the verdict from `result` (deliverable / risky / undeliverable) plus `score` (0-100). `status` is the API call outcome and is "success" even when the address is undeliverable.

fields.description: The email that needs to get verified.
fields.name: email

fields.description: (Optional) Setting the verification mode for the verification job. Default mode is `regular`. > `regular`: The default option for email verification. It does not assume that the domain of the email owner's current company website matches the domain of the email being verified. > `deepverify`: DeepVerify operates on the assumption that the domain of the email owner's current company website matches the domain of the email being verified. This assumption can improve the success rate of verifying accept-all emails. However, it is crucial to obtain the domain for the email owner's current company website from a reliable source, such as the email owner's LinkedIn profile or another trustworthy sales prospecting database. Learn more: [https://support.bounceban.com/article/what-is-deepverify](https://support.bounceban.com/article/what-is-deepverify)

fields.description: (Optional) A webhook target URL specified to receive verification result event in real-time through an HTTP POST request. In case of a failed webhook event delivery, the system will attempt to resend the event up to two additional times within a short interval. For those verifying a substantial volume of emails, it's crucial to ensure that your webhook server is equipped to manage the incoming traffic. Services such as ngrok have been known to encounter issues when dealing with a significant number of events due to inherent limitations. We suggest exploring alternative testing services like TypedWebhook Tools [https://typedwebhook.tools/](https://typedwebhook.tools/) for a more robust solution. Please note that we are not affiliated with this service. > The webhook event will also include the `event-type: single.email_verification_finished` header so you can differentiate between different events. > Please note that the webhook event payload will be in JSON format. ``` { "id": "502abcde", "status": "success", "email": "dev@bounceban.com", "result": "deliverable", "score": 99, "is_disposable": false, "is_accept_all": false, "is_role": true, "is_free": false, "mx_records": [ "alt1.aspmx.l.google.com", "alt2.aspmx.l.google.com", "alt3.aspmx.l.google.com", "alt4.aspmx.l.google.com", "aspmx.l.google.com" ], "smtp_provider": "Google", "verify_at": "2022-11-16T07:21:24.943Z", "credits_consumed": 1.000, "credits_remaining": 375214.000 } ```

fields.description: The unique id returned by every successful request to the [/v1/verify/single](#tag/Single-verification/paths/~1v1~1verify~1single/get) endpoint. > Please consider implementing rate limiting for polling requests to avoid excessive traffic. We recommend capping polling to no more than 10 requests for the same verification `id` within a 5-minute period. After 5 minutes, polling should stop if no results are available, and a new verification request should be initiated instead. > For a more efficient approach, we highly recommend using a webhook event to listen for verification results. You can set this up by providing a callback URL via the `url` parameter in your [/verify/single](#tag/Single-verification/paths/~1v1~1verify~1single/get) API request, allowing results to be sent to your system without the need for repeated polling.
